brief: A GS industrials/materials desk note opens with cross-asset levels (S&P futures flat, Asia up, Europe down on 13-year-low consumer confidence, oil at local highs, gold sub-$4k, 10Y at 4.98%, Fed hold expected) ahead of a big central-bank week. A risk commentary (Privo) argues front-end rates have stabilized (good for risk), energy is too high but more likely to cause chop than a selloff, and credit is the real worry, still flashing yellow-to-red; if credit calms it could be a rally catalyst. This week's test for hyperscalers is capex, backlog conversion, FCF and financing choices, not headline beats; tech flows turned slightly less one-sided (net selling eased). Three earnings-season reads follow: defense is catching a fundamentals-driven bid (LMT, NOC up; watching GD, LHX) into midterms; non-residential construction ex-data-center is broadly improving, setting up CAT this week, with ALLE now top-weighted in the homebuilding index; and European earnings moves have largely happened, so fading the next prints (named pairs) may make more sense. Overnight, WHR, GBX, JBLU and CLW all missed or guided down, each with large implied moves.
